plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero, as they are below stops and do not fit a conservative profile.
Exit all remaining leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU) to reduce overall risk.
Trim QQQI to 20% to maintain single-name limits and free up cash.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio leverage and concentration.
The goal is a stable portfolio with minimal drawdown potential.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a modest ~1.5% monthly return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns, but also limited upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL and SPAL to reduce leveraged ETF exposure, bringing the sleeve within mandate.
Reduce other leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU) to lower overall portfolio leverage.
Buy NET at 4% as a new position, leveraging its strong scanner score and risk/reward.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some exposure to high-potential names while reducing overall leverage.
The goal is consistent growth with managed risk.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly growth, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a reasonable balance between upside and risk.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL, increasing exposure to leveraged ETFs within the aggressive mandate.
Increase positions in other leveraged holdings (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU) to lean into growth.
Buy NET at 6% as a new position, capitalizing on its strong scanner score and risk/reward.
This plan stretches for growth by increasing leverage and concentrating in high-potential assets.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk and daily decay of leveraged ETFs.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly growth, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-beta names, amplifying both upside and drawdown potential. Be aware of higher volatility, potential for larger losses, and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is paramount.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero, as they are below stops and do not fit an income profile.
Exit all remaining leveraged positions (METU, PLTU, MSFU, MUU) to reduce high-beta exposure.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income and low drawdown over growth.
The goal is to park cash for yield with a focus on stability.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% monthly yield, focusing on parking cash for distributions. It eliminates all leveraged and high-beta positions, rotating into income-generating ETFs. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns. Expect very low drawdown but minimal capital appreciation.
